clue.text: Back up! Rugby forward's opponent easily overcome

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shove, as rugby forwards give the scrum to drive it over the try line
second meaning: someone who offers no resistance

explanation.surface: A rugby player shouts at a team-mate while facing a feeble opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union a pushover try is scored when the forwards drive the scrum over the line, so 'Rugby forward's' supports the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushover is informal for a weak rival beaten without effort, while push over is a command to shift along.

clue.text: Write up a record about the scene of miracle cure

indicators.note: in a down clue, written upward means read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the record wraps round the place

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
Cana in Galilee, where water was turned into wine

explanation.surface: A journalist is told to report on the site of a miraculous healing.
explanation.walkthrough: The miracle at Cana was Jesus's first, at a wedding. 'miracle' does double duty, pointing to Cana and qualifying the cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed remedy for every ailment, a cure-all.

clue.text: A spot in the desert at the end of Flecker's Golden Road

definitions.text: at the end of Flecker's Golden Road

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other, here the mark within the desert

parts.note: a desert is a stretch of sand
taken as written
a spot is a mark

explanation.surface: A traveller notes an oasis-like point in a desert at the close of a poet's journey.
explanation.walkthrough: James Elroy Flecker's poem The Golden Journey to Samarkand has the line 'We take the Golden Road to Samarkand'.
explanation.definitionFit: Samarkand, the Silk Road city in Uzbekistan, is the destination named in Flecker's verse.

clue.text: One embracing bachelor — e's disgusting!

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the first word wraps round what follows

parts.note: taken as written
BSc is a Bachelor of Science degree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lone man's slovenly bachelor pad is condemned as revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive to decency, repugnant or revolting.

clue.text: Just ten to do — see about it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cathedral city goes round what precedes

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, so a bishop's see
X is the Roman numeral ten
to act is to do

explanation.surface: Ten tasks remain, and someone must attend to them.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely, in Cambridgeshire, is a favourite crossword one.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and exactly are interchangeable adverbs meaning precisely, as in just right.

clue.text: Refrain from friction about study

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word for friction is written from its end

parts.note: a rub is friction or chafing
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: Advice to stop rubbing something while one works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a verb meaning hold back, but it is the noun: the burden of a song is its chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: Burden is an old name for the chorus or recurring lines of a song, which is what a refrain is.

clue.text: Daisy sweet in this capacity

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a pretty flower or a lovely girl
setter's reading: the song Daisy Bell, where she looks sweet on the seat of a two-person machine

explanation.surface: Praise for a girl called Daisy looking lovely in some role.
explanation.walkthrough: The music-hall song Daisy Bell runs: 'But you'll look sweet upon the seat of a bicycle made for two.'
explanation.definitionFit: The rider of a pedal cycle is a cyclist, the role Daisy fills in the old song.

clue.text: Neat example of, say, rank dandy

indicators.note: say asks for the spoken form of the next word, not its spelling

parts.note: a rank is a row; the fish-egg spelling is said the same
a buck is an old word for a fashionable young man

explanation.surface: A tidy specimen of a smelly fop.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: neat is an old word for horned beasts like cattle, and a roebuck is a fine horned buck, standing in for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A roebuck is a male roe deer, a horned animal loosely offered as an instance of horned livestock.

clue.text: He gives a seat to one standing

definitions.text: He gives a seat to one standing

parts.words: He gives a seat to one standing
parts.note: surface reading: a polite passenger offering a seat on a crowded bus; setter's reading: a candidate standing for parliament, who wins a seat by votes

explanation.surface: A courteous man offers his seat to someone on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics candidates 'stand' for election and win 'seats'.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter in a constituency helps hand a parliamentary seat to the person running for office.

clue.text: Making music and a mint of money

indicators.note: making something out of raw material reshapes it, so these letters are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pop star earns a fortune from songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A mint of money' reads as a fortune, but 'mint' is just letters and 'of money' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Numismatic is the adjective for the study and collecting of coins and currency.

clue.text: What "The Avengers" got, notwithstanding

definitions.meaning: first meaning: avengers got their revenge, they got level
second meaning: as in '... so', in spite of that

explanation.surface: A query about the old TV spy show The Avengers and what it achieved.
explanation.walkthrough: The Avengers was a 1960s British TV series; the quotation marks tempt you toward the show, but any avenger 'gets even'.
explanation.definitionFit: To get even is to take revenge, and even as in 'even so' carries the sense of despite.

clue.text: What takes the money? The electricity bill?

definitions.meaning: setter's reading: the everyday bank account into which money is paid, punning on electric current
surface reading: the bill for a household's power supply

explanation.surface: Grumbling that the electricity bill swallows all one's cash.
explanation.walkthrough: An electricity bill would be an account for current, but the phrase means an ordinary bank account.
explanation.definitionFit: A current account is a standard bank account for day-to-day deposits and payments.

clue.text: Rebellious Jack enrolled in girl's school

indicators.note: someone enrolled in a group is taken inside it, so one name goes within the other

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name
Jack Cade led the Kentish rebellion of 1450

explanation.surface: A wayward boy is sent to a girls' school.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade was the leader of a popular revolt against Henry VI, so 'Rebellious Jack' names him rather than describing a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a school, especially a private or specialised place of learning.

clue.text: Around the North, a lot of fine stuff is available for money

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the goods surround the shorter pieces

parts.note: mercery is the goods of a mercer: silks and fine fabrics
N is the abbreviation for north
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fine goods up north can be had for a price.
explanation.walkthrough: A mercer is a dealer in fine textiles; 'fine stuff' is cloth, not quality in general.
explanation.definitionFit: A mercenary person or soldier works purely for payment, so is for hire to anyone.

clue.text: Tree at start of mouse's trip

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a North American nut tree
second meaning: the opening word of the nursery rhyme in which the mouse ran up the clock

explanation.surface: Where a mouse sets off on a journey, from the foot of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme begins 'Hickory, dickory, dock, the mouse ran up the clock'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hickory is a hardwood tree of the walnut family and the first word of the familiar rhyme.

clue.text: Try too much to make her a cover

indicators.note: to make is to fashion something new, so these letters are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone strains to make a woman a bedspread.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreach is to attempt more than one can manage, overextending oneself.

clue.text: In street Arab girl loses a bird

indicators.note: to lose something is to go without it, so a letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Maud is a girl's name
taken as written; this is the letter dropped
the lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: An Arab girl in a street has lost a pet bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Street Arab' is an old phrase for a homeless child; 'Arab' is not a separate word for the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A mudlark was a child scavenging riverside mud, a dated term for a ragged urchin of the streets.

clue.text: Just a musical instrument

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a piano with vertical strings

explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'only', but it is the adjective for fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright means honourable in conduct, and an upright is the tall domestic piano as opposed to a grand.

clue.text: Like an animal, one gets excited during a row

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a line is a row

indicators.note: something excited is agitated and stirred up, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grows beastly and worked up in the middle of a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel, but it is a line of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means like a lion, so it describes a quality of one particular animal.

clue.text: The ways of devious setters

indicators.note: devious means taking a winding, indirect route, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry comment on the tricks of crossword compilers.
explanation.definitionFit: Streets are roads, and ways is an old word for roads or routes through a place.

clue.text: The spot in which revolutionaries plot changes

indicators.note: in which says the answer lies inside the words that follow, running across them

parts.note: the letters run on from the end of the first word, through the second, into the start of the third

explanation.surface: Revolutionaries gather at a secret place to alter their scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The spot in which revolutionaries plot' reads as a hideout, but the spot is a stain lurking across three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A splotch is a large irregular stain or blot, a kind of mark or spot.

clue.text: Poem composed by our dean

indicators.note: to compose is to put elements in order, so these letters are newly arranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Verses written by the head of the college.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a short French verse form with a refrain and only two rhymes.

clue.text: Regret rising — send in crack troops

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top
in tells us the first word goes inside the troops

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's elite special forces regiment
taken as written

explanation.surface: An officer regrets deploying elite soldiers as a crisis mounts.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAS is the Special Air Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadness is sorrow, the unhappy feeling that comes with regret.

clue.text: Foul-mouthed American Communist

parts.note: surface reading: a swearing left-wing American; setter's reading: sounds like fowl, so a bird named after a US state and coloured like a communist

explanation.surface: A rude, swearing American leftist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul' is said like fowl: the answer is a chicken breed named after the smallest US state, and Red is the usual nickname for a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhode Island Red is a well-known breed of domestic chicken with reddish-brown plumage.

clue.text: Fruit I lug around

indicators.note: things thrown around end up scattered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains about carrying fruit about.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a cross of grapefruit and tangerine.

clue.text: Still identical

definitions.meaning: second meaning: exactly alike in every respect

explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adjective for calm, but it is the adverb meaning nonetheless.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase serves as an adverb for nevertheless and, read literally, describes things that match completely.

clue.text: It's hard to get slippery fish into a pen

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside, so the fish sits within the enclosure

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
the eel is a famously slippery fish

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to coax a wriggling fish into an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely describes something like steel, unyielding and tough, as in a steely gaze.

clue.text: Ought to take one's place in this chain of reasoning

indicators.note: taking someone's place means replacing them, so one word ousts a letter of another

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one; this letter is removed
taken as written, and put where the removed letter was

explanation.surface: A step in an argument: something should take its proper position in the sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughts strung together form a line of reasoning, the mental steps of an argument.
